  February 9, 2023
  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 1
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Steve Costley, Parks & Recreation Director
Date:  January 30, 2023

Subject:  Art in Public Places Application Update

Recommended Motion: Discuss the proposed art piece and provide direction for staff
or Trust For Public Lands to either forward the Commission’s recommendation to the
project manager of the Urban Orchard or return to the artist for changes.

Report Summary: The Parks & Recreation Commission holds a secondary role as the
City of South Gate’s Arts Commission. In this role they approve public art projects that
take place through the “Art in Public Places” ordinance and any other art projects that
are part of public facilities.

Tonight, Trust for Public Lands (TPL) who is partnering with the City of South Gate in
the construction of the Urban Orchard Project is re-presenting to the Commission art
work that will be placed on the City water tower inside the Urban Orchard Park.

The role of the Commission is to determine if the piece presented fits the proposed
location and would be a benefit to the community. Decisions should not be made on
either the proposed artist or the manner in which the project is carried out.

With us tonight will be representatives from TPL who will be making a presentation
about the proposed art project.

 Memorandum

To:  Ana V. Medina, Senior Secretary, City of South Gate

From: Matilda Reyes, Project Manager, TPL

Date: Nov. 2, 2022

Re:  Mural Artwork (Urban Orchard Project) Art Commission Final Approval

We are seeking final approval on the mural design located on the Hawkins Reservoir
adjacent to the Urban Orchard project. On March 10, 2022, we received approval by the
Art Commission to present the two (2) mural concepts to the community. TPL in
collaboration with the City of South Gate conducted and/or attended four (4) events to
gather feedback from the community.
The community selected Option 1. They provided color recommendations and indicated
the words “South Gate” be incorporated in the design. Hector Arias and River Garza, the
mural artists, furthered developed the mural design incorporating the feedback received by
the community.

Mural Location – Hawkins Reservoir in the City of South Gate
(Adjacent to the Urban Orchard project)

   Parks & Recreation Commission Regular Meeting
  February 9, 2023
  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 3
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Glenn Massey, Parks Superintendent
Date:  January 30, 2023
Subject:  Grounds and Facility Maintenance 2nd Quarter Report FY 2022/23

Recommended Motion: Motion to Receive and File

Report Summary: For the Commission’s consideration and review; the following are
details of both Grounds and Facility Maintenance updates for this past quarter.

 Grounds Maintenance

  ❖ Grounds staff 6 assisted with the setup and teardown of the initial Centennial
  event. Along with making sure the trash cans were available and picking up any
  litter. Staff were able to make sure there weren’t any issues as far as Grounds
  Maintenance assistance goes.

  ❖ This quarter we have renovated baseball diamonds 2, 3., 4, and 6.  We are
  currently working on diamond 1.

  ❖ Staff has continued routine procedures such as, pressure washing picnic tables,
  benches, playground areas, handball courts, small quad, bandstand, outside
  restrooms, golf course, senior center, City Hall and other areas as needed, and in
  preparation for rentals. A

  ❖ We are continuing to overseed high traffic areas and fix the irrigation issues
  throughout all City parks.

  ❖ Staff is working on controlling the gopher activity thought all City Parks

  ❖ We continue to comply with CDC recommendations; staff continues servicing and
  beautifying over 180 acres of park land.

  9
 Park Facility Maintenance

  ❖ Our Parks Facility Maintenance division, along with Grounds Maintenance,
  helped plan, set up, clean, maintain, organize, run booths, and be part of history
  by celebrating our City of South Gate 100 Year anniversary on January 21. Four
  Facility Maintenance staff along with six Grounds staff assisted.

  ❖ Even though it’s winter, we are still doing a third daily restroom service to our
  outdoor restrooms due to the high use of SG Park.

  ❖ We have continued the use of Electrostatic Disinfecting Equipment for more
  coverage in our cleaning and disinfecting efforts for both indoor and outdoor
  restroom facilities, along with a pressure washing program. These disinfecting
  and cleaning tools will allow us to use them simultaneously, giving us more
  coverage. Set ups for all events require us to disinfect all tables, chairs, door
  handles, and a/v equipment.

  ❖ Staff is coating outdoor restroom floors with epoxy with the help of Public Works
  to help in keeping the structures sanitary.

  ❖ Since COVID-19 restriction continue being relaxed we have been in full operation
  with classes, as well as private rentals, picnics, sports, and clubs, we continue to
  host several COVID-19 vaccine clinics, testing, and food giveaways for the
  community during this period.

  ❖ The Community Service Worker program continues; we are still limiting intake to
  15 people maximum per day for staff safety.

  ❖ Parks continue to be opened for events, classes, picnics, and sports activities.
  Although pandemic mandates have been relaxed, we remain vigilant in changes
  from local, state, and federal government when addressing the ongoing
  challenges with restroom cleanliness with a weekly restroom disinfecting
  program to mitigate the spread of COVID-19. This entails the use of the C3
  Machine to apply the disinfectants and cleaners. Once the product is sprayed,
  staff scrubs floors, walls, and fixtures to insure thoroughness.

 Staff continues to work hard to keep our parks clean and safe and making sure to keep
 up with any CDC changes and staff will create a plan to service indoor and outdoor
 facilities accordingly.

   Parks & Recreation Commission Regular Meeting
  February 9, 2023
  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 2
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Steve Costley, Director of Parks & Recreation
Date:  January 30, 2023
Subject:  Recreation Program Report - 2nd Quarter Review FY 2022/23

Recommended Motion:  Motion to Receive and File

Report Summary: This report covers recreation programs held during the second quarter of
fiscal year 2022-2023. During these months there is typically less interest in programs due to
the weather and time change.

Partner Organizations (Sports):
AYSO is still in their re-organization phase and has yet to offer any soccer leagues.
SG Aztecs football concluded their season with their end of year banquet at the Girls Club
House. Aztec Cheer teams were in full swing preparing for competition in early 2023.
SGJAA Fall baseball and softball seasons ended successfully and the Winter 22-23 basketball
season has begun with practices held inside the Sports Center Gymnasium.

Fitness:
Our membership program saw the switch of registration software in December from Etrak to
Civic Rec. To allow a smooth transition, memberships were not renewed on Etrak after
November 7 and were not transferred over into Civic Rec, which meant beginning our
membership program without any existing members. We began rebuilding our memberships on
December 12. Despite the pause in memberships, we saw consistent second quarter
attendance compared to previous years, which is an encouraging sign. Our Personal Training
program saw a slight increase from 140 hours to 152 in the second quarter, which is typically
our slowest Personal Training season, given the holidays. We expect hours to continue rising
as we continue to rebuild our memberships. Lastly, we added a new Group Exercise class to
our schedule. Zumba is now being offered on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 11:15am-12:00pm
and has already had positive reviews from our members.

Aquatics:
Even with the changing of the seasons, the Patricia G. Mitchell Swim Stadium continued to see
a lot of traffic due to the many programs we offer year-round. Our Learn-to-Swim programs,
which serve ages 6 months to 100 years, had almost 2,000 registrations. Youth Group Swim
Lessons, our most popular program, had almost 1,000 registrations. Private & Semi-Private
Swim Lessons had almost 800 registrations. Adult Swim Lessons had over 100 registrations
and Adult Fitness Classes (SeniorCise, Aqua Aerobics and Masters Swim) had almost 100
attendees. As one of the only indoor, year-round pools in the area that is open 7 days a week,
our daily attendance numbers remained strong with over 1,300 daily admission attendees and

  11
 almost 1,000 new and renewed Splash Memberships. We saw a slight decrease in the number
of private rentals we had, but an increase in swim team rentals with the addition of the Lynwood
Marlins Swim team. The Patricia G. Mitchell Swim Stadium is now host to three swim teams in
addition to the South Central Swim League’s Fall-Winter league. Hosting the league is
particularly exciting as each individual meet brings in approximately six local teams with over
400 athletes and an additional 900 spectators. Concessions for the meet also serve as a
fundraiser to our partner organization South Gate Aquatics Club, who are the current league
champions and just celebrated their 28th year anniversary!

Youth Sports:
Fall classes again reached full capacity. Football Fundamentals was a newly added class held
over at Legacy High School; this class has created some buzz within our community with many
patrons requesting it become a permanent program in our Youth Sports division. Our weeklong
Winter Sports Camp was held December 19-23, for 3 hours daily. The camp had 18 registered
participants between the ages of 7-12. Participants were taught the fundamentals of soccer,
volleyball, football, baseball, and basketball. Each day ended with friendly scrimmages that the
children really enjoyed, and every registered participant received a camp shirt, medal, and sack
pack.

Adult Sports:
Our Fall Adult Softball Leagues began, we currently have 12 Men’s teams registered for
Thursday evenings (2 divisions) and 17 Co-ed teams registered for Friday evenings (3
divisions). 1st place winners in each of their respective divisions of the Fall season will be
awarded Championship Hoodies. 2nd place winners of each division will be awarded an
insulated water bottle. Our Men’s Basketball season concluded, and the Champions “Go HAM”
were crowned. They were ecstatic with their reversible jerseys and crystal basketball trophy.
Our Sports Center trophy display case is currently in the design process, all Adult Sport
Champions will be displayed. Open play volleyball continues to drive in the players on Tuesday
evenings, the second quarter had a total of 525 drop in participants.

Social Media:
Our total followers are now up to 3,366. In the last quarter we had 5 posts, 86 stories, and 1
reel. We are currently in the recruitment process for a Recreation Marketing Coordinator to
oversee the Social Media Task Force.

Contract Classes:
All Dance, Art and Music classes all filled. We added Cheerleading classes and 2 additional
Tumbling classes to meet the demand from the public. The 3–5 year-old classes are the most
popular and fill quickly, staff is looking into adding more classes for the Spring session.

Youth Classes:
Tot Time is still having difficulties filling classes, had to combine 2 classes into 1, with 15
registered in each class. Due to all schools in SG offering FREE PreK for 4-5 year olds this
affects the registration. Tiny Twos is increasing in registrations and have opened the registration
to 15 per class from 10 and all classes filled quickly.
Cultural Arts:
There was an Art Exhibit “Mi Barrio/ My Neighborhood” that took place in the Gallery from late
October – January for the community. The exhibits are very popular amongst the community,
and they were able to visit the Museum as well. Adult Oil painting is also a popular class that
always fills to capacity.

Special Events:
Halloween Haunt: The annual event was held at SG Park only this year, since Hollydale

  12
 Community is under construction. There were FREE carnival games with candy & prizes as give
aways, costume contest with goodie bags with gift cards as prizes, children’s train ride, and
photo booths. There were around 5,000 in attendance throughout the night.

Tree Lighting:
The annual event took place at City Hall on December 1, 2022. There was entertainment, a visit
from Santa and a tamale give-away for all 250 in attendance.

Santa’s Breakfast:
The event was attended by 325 children and their families. They got to enjoy a pancake &
sausage breakfast, coffee, orange juice/milk. There were also craft projects and themed
coloring papers. Raffles were conducted to take home a Christmas tree or a boy or girl bikes
with helmets. Every child received a present from Santa Claus and were able to take pictures.
The Grinch was also in attendance and gave a gift to all those courageous enough to approach
him.
